# OpenDoc

     new page cannot be forgotten. Edit this file, then run

> OpenDoc is an Apache-2.0 alternative to ONLYOFFICE Docs for documents and
> document collaboration: an embeddable, local-first editor for Word documents,
> and the deterministic Rust engine underneath it, running natively, headless,
> or in the browser as WebAssembly.

OpenDoc is developed by CasualOffice and licensed under Apache-2.0, with no
commercial edition and no licence-gated customisation. The engine, not the
browser DOM, owns document state and layout. Nothing has to run behind the
editor: it opens, edits and saves a document entirely in the browser tab. Host
applications own storage, network, authentication, fonts and product UI policy.
No server, React dependency or collaboration provider is required.

OpenDoc is pre-release. There is no stable public SDK, no tagged release, and
no published npm package or crate yet. It is not a pixel-perfect replacement for
Microsoft Word; per-construct fidelity is graded on the fidelity page below,
and those grades are hand-checked rather than CI-enforced.

## What it does today

- Formats in the browser editor. Open and save: DOCX, ODT, plain text, and a
  normalized JSON snapshot. Open only: RTF (import; there is no RTF writer).
  Export only: PDF with real, selectable text (no tagged PDF, PDF/A or
  clickable links yet), HTML, Markdown, and DOTX. Macro-enabled .docm files are
  refused at open.
- Loss reporting: an import says what it mapped, what it kept verbatim and what
  it lost, and an unedited DOCX can be written back byte-identical.
- Review: comments with replies and resolve; tracked changes with Editing,
  Suggesting and Viewing modes and accept/reject; version history kept locally
  in the browser; Compare shown as an on-page redline.
- Real-time collaboration, experimental: operational-transformation co-editing
  through an optional relay (`opendoc-relay`) that orders and forwards changes
  and never holds the document. Rooms carry a role (viewer, commenter,
  suggester, editor, owner). Remote carets and selections are shown, labelled by
  participant number. Share needs a host-supplied storage provider; the public
  demo has none, so it cannot co-edit or share. The relay has no built-in TLS,
  authentication or rate limiting, and its container image is built locally,
  not published.
- Embedding: a framework-free `<opendoc-editor>` custom element and an iframe
  mount, a capability contract the host decides, an in-page and a cross-origin
  postMessage command surface, and white-labelling from one configuration file.
  The package is buildable from the repository; it is not on npm.
- Phone layout and touch selection in mobile browsers, tested in emulation; not
  yet verified on real devices.

## Site pages

<!-- Generated from each page's own <title> and meta description by
     webapp/tools/build-seo.mjs. Edit the page, not this list. -->
- [OpenDoc — embeddable, open-source ONLYOFFICE Docs alternative](https://opendoc.casualoffice.org/): OpenDoc is an Apache-2.0 alternative to ONLYOFFICE Docs: an embeddable, local-first Word editor on a Rust and WebAssembly engine, with experimental co-editing.
- [Documentation: embed, import and architecture — OpenDoc](https://opendoc.casualoffice.org/docs.html): How to embed the OpenDoc editor, import DOCX, read import dispositions and understand the engine's architecture, plus the full reference document set.
- [Embed the editor — OpenDoc](https://opendoc.casualoffice.org/embedding.html): Embed the OpenDoc editor in your own page: the <opendoc-editor> custom element and a capability contract resolved before the frame's first navigation.
- [DOCX fidelity support matrix — OpenDoc](https://opendoc.casualoffice.org/fidelity.html): OpenDoc's DOCX fidelity, graded per construct against a LibreOffice oracle. Grades are hand-checked: the oracle geometry gate is manual and currently inert.
- [Embed configuration playground — OpenDoc](https://opendoc.casualoffice.org/playground.html): Change a role, withhold a capability, hide a chrome region or set a brand colour, and watch an embedded OpenDoc editor change, then copy the configuration.
- [Target Architecture — OpenDoc](https://opendoc.casualoffice.org/reference/architecture.html): OpenDoc's target architecture: a headless Rust document engine with host adapters, where the DOM, canvas and app state are projections of its model.
- [Context Menu and Shared Command Descriptors — OpenDoc](https://opendoc.casualoffice.org/reference/command-registry.html): The design of OpenDoc's shared command descriptors: one source for the context menu and command palette, with keyboard access and stated disabled reasons.
- [Contributing — OpenDoc](https://opendoc.casualoffice.org/reference/contributing.html): How to contribute to OpenDoc: the development contract, pull request requirements, quality bar, local checks, commit style and Apache-2.0 licensing.
- [Deployment: container images, compose, and configuration — OpenDoc](https://opendoc.casualoffice.org/reference/deployment-containers-and-configuration.html): Deploying OpenDoc: the static editor needs no server; the optional collaboration relay has a Dockerfile, a compose profile and a durable journal.
- [Import Disposition Taxonomy — OpenDoc](https://opendoc.casualoffice.org/reference/disposition-taxonomy.html): How OpenDoc reports what happened to each imported construct, on two axes: how much the model captured, and whether the rest was retained verbatim or lost.
- [DOCX Package Reader — OpenDoc](https://opendoc.casualoffice.org/reference/docx-package-reader.html): How OpenDoc reads a DOCX package: a security-bounded ZIP profile, required parts, path rules, size and expansion limits, and on-demand part reads.
- [Embeddability and the SDK, in three phases — OpenDoc](https://opendoc.casualoffice.org/reference/embeddability-plan.html): OpenDoc's plan for embeddability and the SDK in three phases: one artifact with a capability contract, a host contract, then white-labelling and release.
- [Error Code Registry — OpenDoc](https://opendoc.casualoffice.org/reference/error-code-registry.html): OpenDoc's stable error codes, with their severity, context policy and evolution rules. A code's meaning never changes and a code is never recycled.
- [Project Glossary — OpenDoc](https://opendoc.casualoffice.org/reference/glossary.html): Definitions of the terms used across the OpenDoc runtime, SDK, tests and documentation: product, model, editing, layout, compatibility and quality.
- [Reference documentation — OpenDoc](https://opendoc.casualoffice.org/reference/index.html): Every OpenDoc architecture, design and specification document published on this site, generated from the repository's own Markdown.
- [PDF Export and Print Design — OpenDoc](https://opendoc.casualoffice.org/reference/pdf-export-and-print.html): The design and implementation status of OpenDoc's PDF export and print path: real-text PDF written from the same display list the editor paints.
- [SDK API Specification — OpenDoc](https://opendoc.casualoffice.org/reference/sdk-api-spec.html): The OpenDoc SDK API: the target v1 facade for sessions, commands, snapshots and events, with the Phase 0 subset implemented today marked as such.
- [Security Policy — OpenDoc](https://opendoc.casualoffice.org/reference/security.html): How to report a vulnerability in OpenDoc privately, which versions receive security fixes, and the security boundaries the document engine enforces.

The browser editor is a WebAssembly application, not a document: it is reachable
from the pages above and is deliberately absent from sitemap.xml, because what it
renders to a crawler is application chrome rather than readable prose.

## Technical scope

- OOXML package admission with explicit path, size, expansion, and resource bounds.
- Normalized editable document model with styles, sections, tables, drawings,
  charts, links, fields, notes, headers/footers, comments, revisions,
  bookmarks, and content controls.
- Semantic DOCX writer plus byte-identical reconstruction for unedited packages;
  ODT import and export; RTF import.
- Rust text shaping, pagination, display-list composition, CPU raster rendering,
  real-text PDF export from the same display list, hit testing, model-anchored
  selection, command-based editing, and undo/redo.
- Rust-native, wasm32, and headless execution targets with host-populated font
  and resource seams.
